Input formats

Source: vignettes/articles/input-formats.Rmd
input-formats.Rmd

create_NICHESObject() needs an expression matrix, cell metadata and an LR database. This guide shows how to prepare each one.

library(NICHESv2)
data(NICHESv2_inputs)

Expression matrix

count.mtx is a gene-by-cell matrix, sparse or dense. Row names are gene symbols and column names are cell barcodes.

class(NICHESv2_inputs$count.mtx)
#> [1] "dgCMatrix"
#> attr(,"package")
#> [1] "Matrix"
dim(NICHESv2_inputs$count.mtx)
#> [1] 50 80

The values you pass set what the scores mean. Raw counts give absolute magnitudes, and normalized expression gives relative scores. NICHESv2 uses the matrix as it is, so this choice affects which edges score highest.

Cell metadata

meta.data is a data frame with cell barcodes as row names, matching the matrix columns. What else it needs depends on the mode:

Mode Required columns
"spatial" x and y
"nonspatial" the column named by cell.type.col

Other columns carry through to $cell.meta and appear on each edge in $edge.meta.

head(NICHESv2_inputs$meta.data, 3)
x y nCount_RNA celltype
Cell_1 0.136 0.298 66 TypeA
Cell_2 0.238 0.172 53 TypeA
Cell_3 0.225 0.240 55 TypeA

Several samples

When your data has several samples, set sample.col to the column that identifies them. Each sample is processed separately and the results are merged, so no edges cross samples.

Barcodes must be unique across all samples, and a duplicate stops the merge with an error. Add a prefix first if needed, such as paste0(sample.id, "_", barcode).

LR databases

Pass one of three database names to LRM.db, or your own data frame.

Name Species Needs internet
"connectomedb2025" human, mouse, rat, pig No
"fantom5" human, mouse, rat, pig No
"omnipath" human, mouse, rat Yes, plus OmnipathR

create_NICHESObject() has no default database, so always set LRM.db. Set species to match your data. To look at a database first:

db <- load_LRM_database("connectomedb2025", species = "mouse", verbose = FALSE)
nrow(db)
#> [1] 3252
head(db[, c("ligand", "receptor")], 3)
ligand receptor
A2m Lrp1
Ace Bdkrb2
Adam10 Epha3

Your own database

A custom data frame needs ligand and receptor columns. If they have other names, set ligand.col and receptor.col. Multi-gene complexes are written with underscores, and a pair is dropped if any of its genes is missing from the matrix.

my.db <- data.frame(
  L = c("Gene1", "Gene3"),
  R = c("Gene2", "Gene4_Gene5")
)
obj <- create_NICHESObject(
  count.mtx    = NICHESv2_inputs$count.mtx,
  meta.data    = NICHESv2_inputs$meta.data,
  LRM.db       = my.db,
  ligand.col   = "L",
  receptor.col = "R",
  mode         = "spatial",
  k            = 5L,
  verbose      = FALSE
)
obj$LRM.list
#> [1] "Gene1|Gene2"       "Gene3|Gene4_Gene5"

Seurat objects

extract_NICHESInputs_Seurat() needs the SeuratObject package and reads both V4 and V5 objects, so you don’t need to update an older object first. It returns count.mtx and meta.data.

seu <- SeuratObject::CreateSeuratObject(
  counts    = NICHESv2_inputs$count.mtx,
  meta.data = NICHESv2_inputs$meta.data
)
inputs <- extract_NICHESInputs_Seurat(
  seu, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts", verbose = FALSE
)
dim(inputs$count.mtx)
#> [1] 50 80

Spatial coordinates aren’t copied automatically, because Seurat keeps them with the image. For spatial objects, add them yourself, as shown in the spatial tutorial:

coords <- SeuratObject::GetTissueCoordinates(seurat.obj)
inputs$meta.data$x <- coords[rownames(inputs$meta.data), "x"]
inputs$meta.data$y <- coords[rownames(inputs$meta.data), "y"]

AnnData files

extract_NICHESInputs_AnnData() reads .h5ad files through the rhdf5 package, so Python isn’t needed. layer = "counts" reads the counts layer, and obs.cols limits which metadata columns are kept.

h5ad <- system.file("extdata", "NICHESv2_example.h5ad", package = "NICHESv2")
inputs <- extract_NICHESInputs_AnnData(h5ad, layer = "counts", verbose = FALSE)
dim(inputs$count.mtx)
#> [1] 50 80
colnames(inputs$meta.data)
#> [1] "celltype"   "nCount_RNA" "x"          "y"

Install rhdf5 from Bioconductor:

install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("rhdf5")
